findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
findings.comment:
Inspector observed one live, fast-moving juvenile cockroach near the back door of the facility.

There wasn't any paper towels at the hand-sink in the bar area or the hand-sink across from the cook line. Discussed with PIC and paper towels were provided. Ensure that paper towels are available at every hand-sink to wash hands properly. 

6-301.12: Each HANDWASHING SINK shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; (C) A heated-air hand drying device; (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
Observed there to be no hand soap at the hand-sink in the bar area. Discussed with PIC and hand soap was provided. Ensure that handsoap is available at every handsink in order to properly wash hands. 

6-301.11: Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of 2 adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with a supply of hand cleaning liquid, powder, or bar soap.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
Observed the hand-sink across from the cook-line to be obstructed by a container. The container was removed by the owner. Ensure that hand-sinks are readily available for employees to wash hands and that they are never obstructed. 

5-205.11: (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
The dish machine’s (in kitchen) sanitizing concentration was tested at 0ppm (CL). An employee switched out the sanitizer bucket to correct the violation. The machine was tested again at 100ppm (CL). Ensure that the dish machine is testing at the manufacturer’s recommended sanitizing concentration to properly sanitize dishes. 

4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (A) chlorine shall have minimum temperature (55F), concentration (100ppm), and pH (10). (B) Iodine shall have 68F, pH of 5 or less and concentration of 12.5ppm and 25ppm. (C) Quaternary ammonium shall have 75F, concentration based on label, and water with 500ppm hardness or less. (D) - (E) Meets EPA-label use and regulatory authority approval. (P) (F) Other chemical sanitzers in-use shall have EPA-registered label, display device registration number on devide and is operated and maintained in accordance with manufacturers instructions (Pf)

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment:
Observed several containers of salsa stored in the line cooler to have temperatures between 58F-62F (probed). The cold unit was reset by the owner and the ambient temperature started to drop. An employee stated that the salsas were prepared about 2 hours prior to the inspection. Ice was added to the unit to lower the temperature. The salsa is made from canned tomatoes and is normally cold held after preparation. Be sure that TCS food items are held at 41F or below to ensure proper cold holding temperatures. 

3-501.16: (A) (2) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 41F or less. (B) EGGS not treated to destroy Salmonellae shall be stored at 45F or less.

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
findings.comment:
A line cooler in the kitchen was observed to not be functioning properly. The cooler’s ambient temperatures were between (58F-62F). The cold unit was reset by the owner and the ambient temperature started to drop. Ice was added to the unit to lower the temperature quicker. The cooler’s ambient temperature was again recorded at 36F. Ensure that cold holding equipment is maintained and capable of holding cold food at 41F or below.  

4-301.11: EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures.

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored
findings.comment:
A scoop stored in the sugar container was observed with the handle touching the sugar. Discussed with PIC and the scoop was taken to the dish machine to be cleaned. Ensure that utensils are always stored in a manner where the handle isn't in direct contact with the food to protect against contamination. 

3-304.12: FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored: (A) in FOOD with their handles above top of FOOD and container (B) In non-TCS FOOD (C) On clean portion of FOOD preparation table or cooking EQUIPMENT as long as UTENSIL cleaned with proper frequency (Time/Temp Control Form). (D) In running water with sufficient velocity (E) In clean, protected location if UTENSILS are used only for FOOD not TCS (F) In container of water at least 135F and container is properly cleaned.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.comment:
(REPEAT X3) There was no certified food protection manager present during the inspection. Ensure that a CFPM is present to cover all hours of operation. 

2-102.12: (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting
findings.comment:
The facility could not locate their employee reporting forms. Provided blank copies of employee reporting forms(in English and Spanish) for employees to sign and complete. Ensure that signed employee reporting forms are easily accessible for further routine inspections. 

2-201.11: (A) The PERMIT HOLDER shall require FOOD EMPLOYEES and CONDITIONAL EMPLOYEES to report to the PERSON IN CHARGE information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through FOOD. Report: Symptoms (all P except lesion), diagnosis (all P), and possible exposures (P).  (E) Responsibility of food employee to report symptoms/disease to PIC.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
Observed the dish machine in the outside bar area to have a sanitizing concentration of 0ppm (CL). Discussed with PIC and the sanitizer bottle was replaced. The sanitizing concentration was tested again at 100ppm (CL). Ensure that the dish machine’s sanitizer is maintained at the recommended concentration to properly sanitize dishes. 

4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (A) chlorine shall have minimum temperature (55F), concentration (100ppm), and pH (10). (B) Iodine shall have 68F, pH of 5 or less and concentration of 12.5ppm and 25ppm. (C) Quaternary ammonium shall have 75F, concentration based on label, and water with 500ppm hardness or less. (D) - (E) Meets EPA-label use and regulatory authority approval. (P) (F) Other chemical sanitizers in-use shall have EPA-registered label, display device registration number on devide and is operated and maintained in accordance with manufacturers instructions (Pf)

findings.title: Proper cooling time and temperature
findings.comment:
Observed a container of eggs stored in a drawer cooler along the cookline to be between 81F-87F. PIC noted that the eggs were boiled in the morning and placed in the cooler to cool down. Discussed with PIC alternative techniques to quickly cool eggs. The eggs were discarded by PIC. Ensure that eggs are being cooled properly and are never out of temperature for long periods of time. 

3-501.14: (A) TCS FOOD shall be cooled within in 2 hours from 135F to 70F. Within 6 hours, FOOD shall cool from 135F to 41F or less. (B) TCS FOOD shall be cooled within 4 hours or less if prepared from ingredients at ambient temperature. (C) TCS FOOD received above 45F in compliance with LAWS shall be cooled within 4 hours. (D) Raw EGGS shall be received and immediately placed in EQUIPMENT with air temperature of 45F or less.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
Observed a gallon of whole milk to exceed the manufacturer’s use-by-date in the kitchen’s dessert prep cooler. Discussed with PIC and milk was pulled and discarded. Ensure that milks stored in house over 24 hours never exceed the manufacturer’s use-by-date.  

3-501.17: (A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1 (Pf). (B) Date marking may not exceed manufacturer’s use-by date (Pf). (C) Combined portions of food shall retain the date marking of the earliest-prepared food (Pf). (D) Approved date marking systems (C). (E)  Does not apply to repacked from a bulk container (C). (F) Does not apply to shellstock (C).  (G) Exemptions: prepared deli salads prepared according to 21 CFR 110; hard cheeses (39% moisture); semi-soft cheeses (50% or less); cultured dairy products (yogurt, sour cream, buttermilk); preserved fish (pickled herring, dried/salted); dry, fermented sausages (pepperoni); and salt-cured products (prosciutto and parma).

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
Observed the vent covers of the walk in cooler to be heavily soiled with debris. Discussed with PIC. Ensure that vent covers are cleaned as frequent as necessary to prevent soil buildup. 

4-602.13: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

findings.title: Hot and cold water available; adequate pressure
findings.comment:
Observed the handwashing sink across from the cookline to not have hot water. Owner is aware that the handsink lacks hot water and has been working to get the issue resolved. Ensure that handwashing sinks always have an adequate flow of running hot water to wash hands properly. 

5-103.12: Water under pressure shall be provided to all fixtures, EQUIPMENT, and nonFOOD EQUIPMENT that are required to use water except that water (A) and (B) to a TEMPORARY FOOD ESTABLISHMENT or in response to a temporary interruption of a water supply need not be under pressure.

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used
findings.comment:
Observed an opened can of Pepsi mixed with food items intended for public consumption to be stored in a prep cooler along the cook-line. Discussed with PIC and the Pepsi was discarded. Ensure that personal items are always stored separate from food and drinks that will be served to the public. 

6-403.11: (A) Areas designated for EMPLOYEES to eat, drink, and use tobacco shall be located so that FOOD, EQUIPMENT, LINENS, and SINGLESERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES are protected from contamination. (B) Lockers or other suitable facilities shall be located in a designated room or area where contamination of FOOD, EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES cannot occur.

findings.title: Allergen training as required
findings.comment:
Facility is not allergen trained. Ensure that at least one employee is allergen trained and can show proof of certification for future routine inspections. 

410 ILCS 625/3.07 Sec. 3.07. Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.comment:
(REPEAT X2) There was no certified food protection manager at the start of the inspection. The CFPM arrived shortly afterwards. Ensure that there is always a CFPM present when food preparation is occurring.

2-102.12: (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
An employee was observed to be washing one hand in the hand-washing sink and the other hand was gloved. Employees must scrub both hands together correctly. Ensure that hand-washing is done properly at all times. A follow up will be performed on 1/8/2024

2-301.12: (A) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of arms for at least 20 seconds. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use proper procedure (C) To prevent recontamination, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use barrier to operate faucet handles. (D) Automatic handwashing facility may be used if APPROVED.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
(REPEAT X2) An employee was observed dumping waste water in a metal container into a hand-washing sink. Handwashing sinks are to only be used for hand-washing. Ensure that employees use hand-washing sinks for hand-washing only and never dumping. A follow up will be performed on 1/8/2024.

5-205.11: (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment:
Ice scoops were observed to be soiled inside of the dipper well. Ensure that utensils that are being stored are clean and free of debris. A follow up will be performed on 1/8/2024.

3-302.11: (A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display (P). (3) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by cleaning visibly soiled containers, removing damaged containers, separating washed and unwashed produce (C).

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
Dish machine chlorine final rinse concentration was at 0ppm. A third party repair service came to the facility to repair the machine. Ensure that the chemical sanitizer’s concentration is at the manufacture’s recommendation. Sanitizer concentration at the end of the inspection was 100 ppm. Technician continues to work on repairs and maintenance at the end of the inspection to ensure continued operation. Facility is okay to use the dish machine pending additional follow-up. A follow up will be performed on 1/8/2024.

4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (A) chlorine shall have minimum temperature (55F), concentration (100ppm), and pH (10). (B) Iodine shall have 68F, pH of 5 or less and concentration of 12.5ppm and 25ppm. (C) Quaternary ammonium shall have 75F, concentration based on label, and water with 500ppm hardness or less. (D) - (E) Meets EPA-label use and regulatory authority approval. (P) (F) Other chemical sanitzers in-use shall have EPA-registered label, display device registration number on devide and is operated and maintained in accordance with manufacturers instructions (Pf)

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment:
The temperature of the whipped cream inside the cooler at the bar was 52F and the half and half was 44F. The operator lowered the temperature of the cooler. A second temperature was taken for the whipped cream and the half and half and it remained the same. Ensure that all TCS foods are maintained at 41F or less. A follow up will be performed on 1/8/2024.

3-501.16: (A) (2) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 41F or less. (B) EGGS not treated to destroy Salmonellae shall be stored at 45F or less.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
The whipped cream and half and half in the reach-in cooler at the bar were observed to not be date marked. Multiple desserts in the reach-in cooler in the kitchen were observed to not be date marked. An employee wrote a use-by-date on both products. Ensure that all TCS food products that are being held longer than 24 hours are date marked for a maximum of 7 days after opening.  

3-501.17: (A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1 (Pf). (B) Date marking may not exceed manufacturer’s use-by date (Pf). (C) Combined portions of food shall retain the date marking of the earliest-prepared food (Pf). (D) Approved date marking systems (C). (E)  Does not apply to repacked from a bulk container (C). (F) Does not apply to shellstock (C).  (G) Exemptions: prepared deli salads prepared according to 21 CFR 110; hard cheeses (39% moisture); semi-soft cheeses (50% or less); cultured dairy products (yogurt, sour cream, buttermilk); preserved fish (pickled herring, dried/salted); dry, fermented sausages (pepperoni); and salt-cured products (prosciutto and parma).

findings.title: Consumer advisory provided for raw/undercooked food
findings.comment:
The facility does not have a consumer advisory posted. The facility was provided with two consumer advisory copies. Ensure that consumer advisory is posted at all times. 

3-603.11: (A) If FOOD served raw, undercooked, or without being processed, PERMIT HOLDER shall inform CONSUMERS of RISKS. (B) DISCLOSURE shall include: description and identification (C) REMINDER shall include asterisks regarding safety of items and RISK statement.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Soiled mop heads were observed to be stored with heads on the floor inside of the mop station. Ensure that mop heads are stored in a position that allows them to air dry properly. 

6-501.16: After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to airdry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
The counter behind the dish-machine needs to be caulked to the wall. Ensure that caulking occurs to prevent debris.  

6-101.11: (A) Materials indoor shall be SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE. Areas subject to moisture must be Nonabsorbent. (B) In TEMPORARY FOOD ESTABLISHMENT, floor may be material effectively treated to control dust and mud. Walls and ceilings may be material that protects interior from weather and windblown dust and debris.

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used
findings.comment:
Several personal items including but not limited to glasses, cigarettes, and personal drinks were stored in food preparation areas. Ensure that personal items are stored in designated areas and away from food preparation. 

6-403.11: (A) Areas designated for EMPLOYEES to eat, drink, and use tobacco shall be located so that FOOD, EQUIPMENT, LINENS, and SINGLESERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES are protected from contamination. (B) Lockers or other suitable facilities shall be located in a designated room or area where contamination of FOOD, EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES cannot occur.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.citation_text:
2-102.12 None of the staff working at the time of inspection had proof of food manager certification. Owner has a class scheduled for Sunday, October 8 to get staff certified. Enough staff with food manager certifications need to be available so one is present and working at the facility during all hours of operation. 
NOTE: Employee with food manager certification arrived for work to be present during evening hours of operation.
Person in charge at the time of inspection shall be a certified food protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an accredited program.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.citation_text:
5-205.11 Handwashing sinks were being used as a dump sink and to rinse wiping cloths. Proper use of handwashing sinks was discussed. Ensure staff are educated on proper use and that handwashing sinks are use for handwashing only.
Handwashing sinks are to be accessible at all times and used only for handwashing.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.citation_text:
3-302.11 Raw chicken was observed over steak in the walk-in cooler. Chicken was moved to allow for proper storage.
Food shall be protected from cross contamination by separating foods from each other such as beef, fish, lamb, pork, and poultry during storage, preparation, holding, and display by arranging each type of food in equipment so that cross contamination of one type with another is prevented.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.citation_text:
3-304.11 Soiled utensils, including a pie server, ice cream scoop, and a knife, were observed in the dipper well at the server area. The insert of the dipper well was not present, and moldy buildup was observed in the bottom of the holding well. Utensils were taken to dish area for ware washing. Dipper well was cleaned during inspection. Clean and sanitize utensils between uses, and maintain a clean insert for storage at the dipper well.
Food shall only contact equipment and utensils that are cleaned and sanitized as specified in Parts 4-6 and 4-7 of this Code; single-service and single-use articles; and linens, such as cloth napkins, as specified under § 3 304.13 that are laundered as specified under Part 4-8 of this Code.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
4-501.114 Dish machine chlorine final rinse concentration was observed at 0ppm. Owner primed the sanitizer line continuously for 3 full cycles resulting in a concentration of 100ppm present briefly on the drain board while the concentration on the dish rack was still at 0ppm. After running additional cycles all surfaces were observed without a presence of chlorine residual and consistent concentration of 0ppm was noted. Call for service was made and technicians arrived to provide service during inspection. Tubing was changed and other components of the dish machine were checked to verify proper function.  Final rinse concentration after repairs was at 100ppm.
Chemical sanitizer used in sanitizing solution for manual or mechanical warewashing shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions and be maintained at the concentration as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling. Maintain dish machine final rinse concentration no lower than 50ppm and no higher than 200ppm. Use test strips to verify concentration of bleach solutions.

findings.title: Proper hot holding temperatures
findings.citation_text:
3-501.16 (A)(1) Two pans of rice in a warmer were observed with internal temperatures of 126F and 127F. Rice was just prepared recently and portioned prior to storage in the warmer. The warmer was set near 130F and not maintaining proper hot holding temperature. Rice was reheated to 167F, and maintaining the temperature setting above 135F to allow for proper hot holding was discussed. Setting for warmer was placed above 140F to proper hot hold rice after reheating.
Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control, cooked hot foods that require time/temperature control for safety shall be maintained at 135F/above.

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.citation_text:
3-304.14 Damp wiping cloths were observed on counters throughout the kitchen. Wiping cloths were removed for proper storage during inspection.
Cloths in-use for wiping counters and other equipment surfaces shall be held between uses in a chemical sanitizer solution maintained at proper concentration for the sanitizer product being used.

findings.title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices
findings.citation_text:
5-203.14 Leaks were still present at the plumbing under the dish area 3 part sink. Leaks were observed at the first and middle basins during the last routine inspection. Owner was advised of the leaks during the inspection. 
2) Metal tape and plastic wrapping were were observed on the sprayer head in the dish area. Owner stated they have a part on order, and the sprayer will be repaired once the part is available. 
Provide proper plumbing repairs by next routine inspection. 
A plumbing system shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.citation_text:
6-501.12 Floor drain was heavily soiled with buildup of mold and general debris under the soda machine in the server area. Owner was advised and took a picture of the conditions observed at the time of inspection. Clean the floor drain in question and all drains throughout the facility as needed to eliminate buildup.
Physical facilities shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean

findings.title: All food employees have food handler training
findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625  Sec. 3.06 Proof of food handler certifications were not available for staff. Ensure all staff that do not complete food manager course are food handler certified by next routine inspection. Options for online food handler course were discussed.
All food handlers, other than someone who has a food manager certification, shall receive or obtain training in basic food handling principles as outlined in Subpart M of the Illinois Food Code.

findings.title: Allergen training as required
findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625 Sec. 3.07 Proof of allergen certification was not available for staff. Ensure all certified food managers also complete an allergen course, and maintain copies of certification on-site with all other certifications. All certified food managers need to complete the food allergen awareness training by the next routine inspection to ensure a CFM with allergen certification is on-site during all hours of operation.
Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.citation_text:
2-301.14 Employee working in dish area went from handling soiled dishes to handling clean dishes without a hand wash in between. Employee was educated on handwashing between tasks. Managers on duty were advised on eduction provided to employee and asked to revisit proper handwashing between tasks with all staff.
Food Employees shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in food preparation including working with exposed food, clean equipment and utensils, and unwrapped single-service and single-use articles. Hands shall also be washed after engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands and after handling soiled dishes and prior to handling clean dishes.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.citation_text:
3-501.17 (B) Multiple prepared foods were once again observed with date marks indicating a time frame for use longer than 7 days. Dates were corrected at the time of inspection and staff were re-educated about date marking. An educational spot check will be conducted at the end of the month to revisit date marking and ensure foods are properly dated.
Except as specified in (E) -(G) of this section, refrigerated, ready to eat TCS food prepared and packaged by a food processing plant shall be clearly marked, at the time the original container is opened and if the food is held for more than 24 hours, to indicate the date or day by which the food shall be consumed on the premises, sold, or discarded, based on the temperature and time combinations specified in  (A). The day the original container is opened in the food establishment shall be counted as Day 1, and the day or date marked by the food establishment may not exceed a manufacturer’s use-by date if the manufacturer determined the use-by date based on food safety.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.citation_text:
4-302.14 Facility did not have chorine test strips available for use. Inspector provided a small amount in-order to educate and demonstrate testing at the routine inspection on 5/23/23. Last of those test strips were just used, and the only other strips available for use were for quat sanitizer, which is not used at the facility. Quat strips were expired and discarded. Additional chlorine test strips were provided for use at the facility. Ensure chlorine test kits are maintained and available for use. 
A test kit that accurately measures the concentration of sanitizing solutions in mg/L shall be provided.

findings.title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices
findings.citation_text:
5-203.14 Leaks were still present at the first and middle basins of the dish area triple sink. Look below the basins. Leaks appear to be along the handle for the drain plug and possibly other junctures within the plumbing. Provide proper repairs. 
A plumbing system shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: All food employees have food handler training
findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625  Sec. 3.06 Proof of food handler certifications were not available for any staff. Certifications were said to be in the office during the previous inspection. Certifications were not provided during inspection again today, and management had access to the office today. Ensure all staff complete food handler certification and that copies are maintained on-site.
All food handlers, other than someone who has a food manager certification, shall receive or obtain training in basic food handling principles as outlined in Subpart M of the Illinois Food Code.

findings.title: Allergen training as required
findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625 Sec. 3.07 Proof of allergen certification was not available for CFM working at the time of inspection. Ensure all certified food managers also complete an allergen course, and maintain copies of certification on-site with all other certifications. All certified food managers need to complete the food allergen awareness training by the next routine inspection to ensure a CFM with allergen certification is on-site during all hours of operation.
Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter.

findings.title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties
findings.citation_text:
2-102.11 (A), (B) & (C)(1), (4)-(16) Multiple priority items were observed during the inspection today. See violations 8, 9, 13, 15, 16, 19, 22, & 23 for details. Chlorine test kit was not available for checking bleach solutions. Bleach solutions were initially at 0ppm after preparation, and upon further investigation the bottle of bleach at the bar used to make solutions was already diluted product observed at 200ppm. Hand sanitizer was present in three different hand soap dispensers. Whipped topping and liquid egg were stored in a cooler that was holding at 77F and not working properly for quite some time. Person in charge at time of inspection did not have access to paperwork inspectors needed to review, including certifications and employee health documentation. A certified food manager was not on-site to oversee operations at the time of inspection. Active managerial controls were discussed and will be revisited at follow-up inspection.
Based on the risks inherent to the food operation, during inspections and upon request the PIC shall demonstrate to the regulatory authority knowledge of foodborne disease prevention, application of the hazard analysis and critical control points, and the requirements of the Code.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.citation_text:
2-102.12 None of the staff working at the time of inspection had proof of food manager certification. PIC stated they have a food handler certification but did not have proof of certification with them at the time of inspection. Enough staff with food manager certifications need to be available so one is present and working at the facility during all hours of operation, including morning prep prior to opening. 
Person in charge at the time of inspection shall be a certified food protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an accredited program.

findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting
findings.citation_text:
2-103.11 (O) Employee health documents were said to be in the office but PIC was unable to unlock the door during inspection. Owner and management need to ensure access to employee health documents for ease in reference during inspections. Documents need to be available for viewing by inspectors at time of follow-up inspection.
The person in charge shall ensure that food employees are informed in a verifiable manner of their responsibility to report in accordance with law, to the person in charge, information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through food, as specified under  2-201.11(A).

findings.title: Procedures for responding to vomiting and diarrheal events
findings.citation_text:
2-501.11 Written procedure for responding to diarrhea/vomit incident was not available with other employee health documents. Owner and management need to ensure access to employee health documents, including cleanup policy for norovirus. Cleanup policy needs to be available for viewing by inspectors at time of follow-up inspection.
A food establishment shall have written procedures for employees to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events that involve the discharge of vomitus or fecal matter onto surfaces in the food establishment. The procedures shall address the specific actions employees must take to minimize the spread of contamination and the exposure of employees, consumers, food, and surfaces to vomitus or fecal matter.

findings.title: Proper eating, tasting, drinking, or tobacco use
findings.citation_text:
2-401.11 Approximately 6 bottles, coffee cups, and glasses with personal drinks were observed throughout prep areas intermixed with food and equipment. One of the cooks was also observed actively drinking from their beverage as they were taking tortillas to the walk-in cooler from the cook line. Handwashing and personal beverage consumption were discussed as was proper storage of personal drinks. All drinks were removed from the prep area and discarded. 
Food employees may drink from a closed beverage container if the container is handled to prevent contamination of the employee’s hands; the container; and exposed food; clean equipment, utensils, and linens; unwrapped single-service and single-use articles; or other items needing protection cannot result.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.citation_text:
2-301.14 Employees were not washing hands between tasks as needed and missed several opportunities for handwashing. One employee was observed moving a garbage can and proceeded to prep area without a handwash. Upon arrival one employee on the cook line was observed handling their cell phone in the prep area. Another employee was also observed using a cloth apron to wipe their hands. Proper handwashing between tasks was discussed, and employees were later observed washing hands during inspection. When, where, and how to wash hands will be revisited at a later date during an educational inspection as well.
Food Employees shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in food preparation including working with exposed food, clean equipment and utensils, and unwrapped single-service and single-use articles. Hands shall also be washed after engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands

findings.title: No bare hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed
findings.citation_text:
3-301.11 (B) Handles of ice scoops were observed down inside ice bins in direct contact with ice at the soda machine in the server area and at the bar. Proper scoop storage was discussed. Ensure storage with handles up out of ice to avoid barehand contact. 
Except when washing fruits and vegetables as specified under §3-302.15 or as specified in  (D) and (E) of this section, food employees may not contact exposed, ready-to-eat food with their bare hands and shall use suitable utensils such as deli tissue, spatulas, tongs, single-use gloves, or dispensing equipment.

findings.title: No bare hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed
findings.citation_text:
3-301.11 Employee was observed having barehand contact with limes being cut for garnish. Handwashing and glove use were discussed. Employee washed hands and put on gloves to prepare fresh limes. 
Except when washing fruits and vegetables as specified under §3-302.15 or as specified in  (D) and (E) of this section, food employees may not contact exposed, ready-to-eat food with their bare hands and shall use suitable utensils such as deli tissue, spatulas, tongs, single-use gloves, or dispensing equipment.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.citation_text:
6-301.11 Soap dispensers at three handwashing sinks had sanitizer in them instead of soap. Sanitizer was removed and hand soap provided. Ensure staff are properly educated on what product to use, especially if English is a second language and product label is not in Spanish.
Each handwashing sink shall be provided with a supply of hand cleaning liquid, powder, or bar soap.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.citation_text:
6-301.12 Paper towels at bar handwashing sink were not dispensing. Roll was almost empty and in need of replacing. Providing a fresh roll of paper towels allowed for proper dispensing. 
Each handwashing sink shall be provided with Individual, disposable towels or another approved drying option.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.citation_text:
5-205.11 Handwashing sinks were being used as dump sinks and to fill a sani-bucket in the kitchen. Proper use of handwashing sinks was discussed. Ensure staff are educated on proper use and that handwashing sinks are use for handwashing only.
Handwashing sinks are to be accessible at all times and used only for handwashing.

findings.title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated
findings.citation_text:
3-101.11 Strawberries in the prep cooler were dried out and moldy. Strawberries were discarded. 
Food shall be safe, unadulterated, and honestly presented as specified under 3-601.12.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.citation_text:
3-304.11 Can opener blade was soiled with encrusted debris. Can opener was taken to dish area to be cleaned and sanitized.
Food shall only contact equipment and utensils that are cleaned and sanitized as specified in Parts 4-6 and 4-7 of this Code; single-service and single-use articles; and linens, such as cloth napkins, as specified under § 3 304.13 that are laundered as specified under Part 4-8 of this Code.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.citation_text:
3-304.15(A) Employees were observed using gloves improperly. Multiple surfaces were touched and staff were going between tasks without glove changes. Proper glove use was discussed, and staff were observed making effort to properly use gloves for remainder of inspection. 
Single use gloves shall be used for only one task, used for no other purpose, and discarded when damaged or soiled, or when interruptions occur in the operation.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.citation_text:
3-302.11 Raw chicken was stored over tortillas and shell eggs in the walk-in cooler. Chicken was moved to allow for proper storage under ready to eat foods during inspection.
Corn starch was also uncovered in the dry storage area. Ensure bulk storage bins for powders and other foods are properly covered to protect from potential cross contamination between uses.
Food shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display by separating raw animal foods from ready to eat foods.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
4-601.11 Several soiled utensils and scoops were observed on the cook line and in prep areas. Mixer was also observed put away soiled after use. All items were removed for cleaning during inspection. Ensure food contact surfaces are properly cleaned and sanitized between uses.
Food contact surfaces shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
4-602.11 Soda guns at bars were observed with varying amounts of mold buildup. Soda guns at outside bar had significant buildup and were in need of cleaning. Ensure soda guns and holders are cleaned daily.
Equipment such as beverage dispensing nozzles shall be cleaned at a frequency specified by the manufacturer, or absent manufacturer specifications, at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil or mold

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
4-501.114 Freshly prepared bleach solutions in kitchen were observed at 0ppm chlorine. Upon further investigation the bottle of bleach at the bar used to make solutions was already diluted product observed at 200ppm. Concentrated bleach was used to prepare solutions at proper concentration of 200ppm.
Chemical sanitizer used in sanitizing solution for manual or mechanical warewashing shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions and be maintained at the concentration as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.citation_text:
3-501.16 (A)(2) Whipped topping and liquid egg whites were at 77F in a reach-in cooler on the server line that was not in operation for quite some time. Ensure staff are properly trained to recognize non-functioning coolers and not place TCS foods in equipment that is not able to maintain product at 41F/below. 
Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as a public health control, cold TCS foods shall be maintained at 41F/below.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.citation_text:
3-501.17 (B) Multiple prepared foods were observed with date marks indicating a prep date of 5/19 and use by date of 5/26. Proper time frame of 7 days for use or discard was discussed. Labels are quite nice that are in use but need to reflect proper 7 day time frame for use. Labeling was discussed and will be revisited at follow-up inspection.
Except as specified in (E) -(G) of this section, refrigerated, ready to eat TCS food prepared and packaged by a food processing plant shall be clearly marked, at the time the original container is opened and if the food is held for more than 24 hours, to indicate the date or day by which the food shall be consumed on the premises, sold, or discarded, based on the temperature and time combinations specified in  (A). The day the original container is opened in the food establishment shall be counted as Day 1, and the day or date marked by the food establishment may not exceed a manufacturer’s use-by date if the manufacturer determined the use-by date based on food safety.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment:
4-303.11 No sani-buckets were available on the cookline, bar, or dish area despite preparation activities being underway. Sani-buckets were created during the inspection. 
Sanitizer shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation.
findings.citation_text:
4-302.14 Facility did not have test strips available for dish machine and sani-bucket monitoring. Inspector provided a small amount in-order to educate and demonstrate testing. Provide test kit for bleach and ensure staff are properly educated on testing. 
A test kit that accurately measures the concentration of sanitizing solutions in mg/L shall be provided.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
Hot and cold water available; adequate pressure
findings.citation_text:
5-103.12 No water is available at the hand sink on the wait line. See that hot and cold water is supplied at this hand sink. 
Hot and cold water under pressure shall be provided to all fixtures, equipment, and nonfood equipment that are required to use water.

findings.title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices
findings.citation_text:
5-203.14 A leak is observed at the first and middle basins of the dish area triple sink. Look below the basins. Showed dish operator. Repair leaks. 
A plumbing system shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.citation_text:
6-501.12 (A) The floor has several areas where water from cleaning activities has started ponding. See that water for floor washing is removed/squeegeed as part of the cleaning process. Do not allow surfaces to create a slip hazard or water source for pests. 
Physical facilities shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean

findings.title: All food employees have food handler training
findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625  Sec. 3.06 Proof of food handler certifications were not available for any staff. Certifications were said to be in th office,but PIC at time of inspection did not have access. Ensure staff have access to certifications and other required paperwork for review during inspections. 
All food handlers, other than someone who has a food manager certification, shall receive or obtain training in basic food handling principles as outlined in Subpart M of the Illinois Food Code.

findings.title: Allergen training as required
findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625 Sec. 3.07 Proof of allergen certification was not available for staff. Ensure all certified food managers also complete an allergen course, and maintain copies of certification on-site with all other certifications. All certified food managers need to complete the food allergen awareness training by the next routine inspection to ensure a CFM with allergen certification is on-site during all hours of operation.
Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter.

findings.title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties
findings.comment:
2-102.11: Based on the RISKS inherent to the FOOD operation, PIC shall demonstrate knowledge by:  (A) Having no Priority Foundation items; (B) Being a CFM; OR (C) Responding correctly questions as they relate to the specific FOOD operation. The areas of knowledge include C1 through C16.  

All violations were corrected promptly; however, this violation was marked due to the number of priority and priority foundation violations observed during the inspection. Employees are going to attend a training conducted by MJ Kellner at the end of November. Ensure employees are continually trained on food safety.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
Observed employees not wash their hands before donning gloves and when changing tasks. Additionally, an employee was told by inspectors to wash his hands after returning from the bathroom. Employees must wash their hands when changing tasks, before food preparation, and when donning gloves. Education was provided during the inspection. 

2-301.14: FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including (A)-(I) any activities that may have contaminated the hands.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
The hand sink on the south side of the cook line was blocked by a speaker, and a cart of drink glasses was sitting in front of the dish area hand sink, which made it difficult for dish employees to wash their hands. These items blocking the hand sinks were moved during the inspection. Ensure nothing is blocking or inside of the hand sinks so they are maintained accessible at all times for employee use. 

5-205.11: (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions.

findings.title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated
findings.comment:
Moldy strawberries and rotting tomatoes were observed in the walk in cooler. Food must be gone through frequently to check for food integrity. Ensure food in poor condition is discarded. The strawberries and tomatoes were discarded during the inspection. 

3-101.11: FOOD shall be safe, unADULTERATED, and, honestly presented.

findings.title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated
findings.comment:
Severely dented cans (that were also past the expiration date) were observed in the kitchen. Cans that are severely dented must be discarded. The can was discarded during the inspection. Ensure cans are checked regularly for package integrity frequently.  

3-202.15: FOOD packages shall be in good condition and protect the integrity of the contents so that the FOOD is not exposed to ADULTERATION or potential contaminants.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment:
Chicken was observed stored above beef in the drawer cooler at the cook line. Food storage was discussed with the cooks and the manager. Chicken was moved to the bottom drawer cooler during the inspection. 

3-302.11: (A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display (P). (3) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by cleaning visibly soiled containers, removing damaged containers, separating washed and unwashed produce (C).

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
The dish machine and sani buckets at the bar had a concentration of 0ppm of chlorine at the start of the inspection. Sani buckets were remade and MJ Kellner serviced the dish machine during the inspection. The dish machine had a concentration of 50ppm. 

4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (A) chlorine shall have minimum temperature (55F), concentration (100ppm), and pH (10). (B) Iodine shall have 68F, pH of 5 or less and concentration of 12.5ppm and 25ppm. (C) Quaternary ammonium shall have 75F, concentration based on label, and water with 500ppm hardness or less. (D) - (E) Meets EPA-label use and regulatory authority approval. (P) (F) Other chemical sanitzers in-use shall have EPA-registered label, display device registration number on devide and is operated and maintained in accordance with manufacturers instructions (Pf)

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
Soda nozzles were observed soiled with mold and debris at both bars. Ensure soda nozzles are cleaned frequently so they are maintained cleaned. The soda nozzles were cleaned during the inspection. 

4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
A container of beans and meat were observed past the 7 day date marking in the walk in cooler. The dates on the items had dates of 11/5 and 11/6 respectively. Also, a can of olives was observed past the manufacturer’s date marking. The items were discarded during the inspection. All TCS foods must be date marked with a 7 day date marking if held for more than 24 hours.

3-501.17: (A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1 (Pf). (B) Date marking may not exceed manufacturer’s use-by date (Pf). (C) Combined portions of food shall retain the date marking of the earliest-prepared food (Pf). (D) Approved date marking systems (C). (E)  Does not apply to repacked from a bulk container (C). (F) Does not apply to shellstock (C).

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
The walk in cooler fan and gaskets in prep coolers in the front of the kitchen were soiled. Ensure these surfaces are cleaned so soil does not accumulate on these surfaces. 

4-602.13: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Caulking was missing and coming off of the dish area sink near the sprayers. Ensure caulking is replaced so these areas are smooth and easily cleanable. 

6-101.11: (A) Materials indoor shall be SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE. Areas subject to moisture must be Nonabsorbent. (B) In TEMPORARY FOOD ESTABLISHMENT, floor may be material effectively treated to control dust and mud. Walls and ceilings may be material that protects interior from weather and windblown dust and debris.
